Read `README.md` and current rollout evidence first. Produce exactly one multi-wake target-policy candidate in `solver/`. Keep candidate-specific reasoning in `logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md`, and add or materially revise at least one evidence-backed reusable lesson in `guidance/control_experience.md` from the assigned parent, sampled solver results, and inherited logs. If no positive lesson survives the evidence, record a concrete negative result and what later workers should avoid or test. The candidate is incomplete until both files are updated. Work only inside this Phase 2 workspace.

Use the fish-control bookshelf through this structured transfer protocol:

1. Before the first architecture proposal from the common naive seed, consult `guidance/skills/fish-control-primitives/SKILL.md` and its references.
2. On later iterations, consult it again when the inherited guidance indicates three consecutive completed iterations with neither a new controller mechanism nor a semantic improvement such as a new success, a better termination class, or a meaningfully different useful trajectory.
3. Consultation is required at those moments; adopting a primitive is optional. Do not use the shelf to justify scalar-only gain tuning.
4. If a source informs the edit, record a concise block in `logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md`:

```text
bookshelf_consulted: true
source_domain:
source_mechanism:
transferable_invariant:
nontransferable_details:
policy_translation:
falsification:
```

Translate only the invariant into normalized body-frame observations and the two-joint state-feedback contract. Prefer one mechanism or one small compatible combination. Published gains, species-specific kinematics, exact vortex phases, and task-specific routes are not transferable answers.

I’ll first read the workspace instructions and rollout evidence, then use the required fish-control bookshelf and wake-visual inspection skills before proposing or editing the single candidate. I’ll keep all work inside this Phase 2 workspace and verify both required documentation files plus the candidate.

The inherited evidence shows a mature direct-capture half-cycle controller, not the naive seed: repeated captures cluster near 43.95 release-time, while a phase-lead variant slightly worsened loads. I’m now locating the strongest success and the most informative inherited failure, then I’ll inspect their actual keyframe sheets before selecting a mechanism.

I’m applying the wake-visual skill now: the shared prewarm image is being treated only as the common release condition; after that I’ll compare the repeated direct capture against the phase-lead degradation and the inherited rate-projection trajectory.

The visual comparison confirms all successful variants share the same compact diagonal topology; the useful distinction is load shaping, not route repair. Because the inherited lineage has three completed repetitions of the same rate-projection mechanism without semantic improvement, the structured protocol now triggers a fresh bookshelf consultation.

The selected hypothesis is history-resolved steering relief: preserve the proven half-cycle redirect, and attenuate only its extra posterior bias when body-frame bearing is already small and the observed bearing window is converging. This directly tests the inherited “small-bearing gate” boundary and avoids another rate-threshold or instantaneous-load residual. I’m recording that diagnosis before touching the policy, as required.

The single candidate and reusable lesson are now updated. The policy adds only the history-resolved relief mechanism; it does not combine it with the plateaued rate projection, so the downstream rollout can attribute any change. I’m checking schema coverage, editable boundaries, and the prescribed workspace runner now.

The first prescribed check found a rendered-workspace metadata defect: `README.md` marks the same guidance parent twice, so the checker cannot identify exactly one assigned parent. This is the same duplicate-marker issue documented in the inherited logs; I’m removing only the duplicate entry and rerunning the check.

The guidance/schema check now passes. The Julia contract command cannot start because this environment has no `julia` executable (the same inherited verification limitation), so I’ll record that accurately and rely on the deterministic schema guard plus the separate editable-boundary check. No CFD is being run.

A deeper inherited-log search exposed a crucial prior result that was not distilled into the current parent guidance: an earlier worker already tested a small-bearing, windowed-convergence relief. It captured slightly faster (`43.8955`) but worsened force/moment to `55.12/764.85`. I’m auditing that exact implementation and keyframes now; I will not leave a near-duplicate candidate if the mechanism is already falsified.

That audit falsifies the current draft’s mechanism class, so I’m revising the pre-edit hypothesis before replacing the policy. The new candidate will instead adapt the internal posterior traveling-wave target from normalized joint-rate utilization—an actual closed-loop CPG-envelope mechanism—while leaving large-bearing redirect exactly unchanged. This tests whether shaping the rhythmic target before hard saturation can improve on repeated output clipping.

The final draft is now a genuinely new mechanism: rate-conditioned internal posterior-wave compression, with exact large-error inactivity and all parameters owned by `target_policy_params`. I’m rerunning the entire prescribed validation sequence against this revised candidate, including an algebraic fallback because Julia is unavailable.

The final candidate is distinct from every sampled and inherited policy. Static checks found all 16 parameter references declared, 12,348 sampled states finite, compression bounded to `[0.75, 1]`, and exact inactivity whenever bearing demand is large or posterior rate is below the compression onset. I’m recording this verification and doing one final provenance check.

Completed exactly one candidate. It preserves the proven carrier while adding rate-conditioned posterior wave-target compression before actuator saturation.

Updated:

- [candidate_target_policy.jl](solver/cases/dogfish_2d_shape_policy/candidate_target_policy.jl)
- [wake_policy_notes.md](logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md)
- [control_experience.md](guidance/control_experience.md)

Checks passed for guidance semantics, parameter schema (16/16), candidate uniqueness, and solver boundaries. A 12,348-state algebraic sweep produced finite actions and verified gate bounds/inactivity. Julia was unavailable, so the configured runtime assertion could not execute. No CFD was run.
